newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: ABN AMRO to cut 50 jobs in Frankfurt.
newsitem.headline: ABN AMRO to cut 50 jobs in Frankfurt.

text.p: Dutch bank ABN AMRO NV said on Monday it planned to shed 50 jobs at its Frankfurt unit as part of a reorganisation of its underperforming German operations.
Spokesman Tanno Massar confirmed a report in the Dutch daily Het Financieele Dagblad that the reorganisation would result in the loss of 50 positions at Frankfurter Kredietbank.

He also confirmed that its German lending activities, currently spread across 10 offices, would be centralised in Frankfurt and that the deadline for lifting return on equity in Germany to 12 percent from the current three percent had been put back to 2000 from 1998.
ABN AMRO said in its 1996 annual report that the performance of its German operations fell significantly short of expectations in 1996 after improving in 1995.
The bank has been restructuring them for two years.

Germany, which is considered by analysts to have an over-crowded banking sector, has proved to be a tough market for foreign players because of shrinking margins and the reluctance of clients to leave German banks.
ABN AMRO has about 1,000 staff in Germany, of which 220 are employed by its subsidiary Frankfurter Kredietbank.
ABN AMRO has said it aims to operate as a universal bank in Germany, in the corporate market and in private banking.

Dutch financial services giant ING Groep has identified Germany as a potential market for expansion as it attempts to beef up its European banking operations outside of the Netherlands ahead of the advent of a single currency.

Dutch co-operative group Rabobank said in June it was transferring the assets of its independent Rabobank Deutschland AG unit to Rabobank Nederland to give the German unit access to the parent company's AAA credit rating.
